Zayadina.question: In _____, Sa'd, the eldest Zaydani sheikh and hitherto Daher's key political adviser, conspired with Uthman and the Banu Saqr, with backing from governor Uthman Pasha of Damascus, to eliminate and rep
Zayadina.fact: In 1761, Sa'd, the eldest Zaydani sheikh and hitherto Daher's key political adviser, conspired with Uthman and the Banu Saqr, with backing from governor Uthman Pasha of Damascus, to eliminate and replace Daher.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The plan was detected and Daher turned _____ against Sa'd, having the former assassinate the latter in exchange for control of Shefa-Amr
Zayadina.fact: As early as 1753, Uthman rebelled and sought refuge in Jenin, stronghold of the Jarrars, where he attempted to undermine Daher's rule. In 1761, Sa'd, the eldest Zaydani sheikh and hitherto Daher's key political adviser, conspired with Uthman and the Banu Saqr, with backing from governor Uthman Pasha of Damascus, to eliminate and replace Daher.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Uthman was not awarded with _____-Amr on that occasion due to the opposition of the village's inhabitants
Zayadina.fact: The plan was detected and Daher turned Uthman against Sa'd, having the former assassinate the latter in exchange for control of Shefa-Amr. Uthman was not awarded with Shefa-Amr on that occasion due to the opposition of the village's inhabitants.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Rebellions intensified throughout the 1760s, as _____'s sons sought to strengthen their positions in anticipation of their aging father's death
Zayadina.fact: The plan was detected and Daher turned Uthman against Sa'd, having the former assassinate the latter in exchange for control of Shefa-Amr. Uthman acceded and Daher thus neutralized his last major rival within the Zayadina.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Uthman renewed demands for _____-Amr, besieging it with his brothers Ahmad and Sa'd al-Din
Zayadina.fact: Uthman renewed demands for Shefa-Amr, besieging it with his brothers Ahmad and Sa'd al-Din.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: When the brothers were repulsed by the local defenders, they barricaded in the citadel of _____, where Salibi mediated on their behalf with Daher
Zayadina.fact: When the brothers were repulsed by the local defenders, they barricaded in the citadel of Tiberias, where Salibi mediated on their behalf with Daher.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The mediation failed and the brothers gained the backing of the _____, but the Bedouins withdrew their support after Daher offerred them tax incentives
Zayadina.fact: The mediation failed and the brothers gained the backing of the Banu Saqr, but the Bedouins withdrew their support after Daher offerred them tax incentives.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Daher afterward had _____ imprisoned in Haifa for a half year before exiling him to a village near Safed, having deprived him of his weapons, horses and men
Zayadina.fact: Uthman renewed demands for Shefa-Amr, besieging it with his brothers Ahmad and Sa'd al-Din. Daher afterward had Uthman imprisoned in Haifa for a half year before exiling him to a village near Safed, having deprived him of his weapons, horses and men.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Uthman gained the support of Druze and _____ factions and renewed his rebellion, but Daher defeated him with the support of his other sons Ali and Ahmad
Zayadina.fact: Uthman gained the support of Druze and Metawali factions and renewed his rebellion, but Daher defeated him with the support of his other sons Ali and Ahmad.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Afterward, Ali revolted against Daher for the latter's successive refusals to cede him _____ and Deir al-Qassi
Zayadina.fact: Afterward, Ali revolted against Daher for the latter's successive refusals to cede him Deir Hanna and Deir al-Qassi. Ali's rebellion persisted as he sought control of Deir Hanna and after multiple clashes, Daher ceded control of the village for payment.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Ali's rebellion persisted as he sought control of _____ and after multiple clashes, Daher ceded control of the village for payment
Zayadina.fact: Afterward, Ali revolted against Daher for the latter's successive refusals to cede him Deir Hanna and Deir al-Qassi. Ali's rebellion persisted as he sought control of Deir Hanna and after multiple clashes, Daher ceded control of the village for payment.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: He ended his rebellion after _____ mobilized against him, but was given Deir al-Qassi
Zayadina.fact: Uthman gained the support of Druze and Metawali factions and renewed his rebellion, but Daher defeated him with the support of his other sons Ali and Ahmad. Afterward, Ali revolted against Daher for the latter's successive refusals to cede him Deir Hanna and Deir al-Qassi.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: He and Sa'id (full brothers) then rebelled again when Daher refused to grant Sa'id control of Tur'an and _____, but this was settled in mediation and the villages were ceded
Zayadina.fact: He and Sa'id (full brothers) then rebelled again when Daher refused to grant Sa'id control of Tur'an and Hittin, but this was settled in mediation and the villages were ceded.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The rebellions by Daher's sons were nearly always backed by the governor of Damascus, _____, who sought to sustain the internal dissent to weaken Daher
Zayadina.fact: The rebellions by Daher's sons were nearly always backed by the governor of Damascus, Uthman Pasha, who sought to sustain the internal dissent to weaken Daher. The latter lodged complaints to the imperial government about Uthman Pasha's support for his rebellious sons at least once in 1765.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The rebellions of the 1760s also often drew in rival factions among the _____ and the Shihab-led Druze of Mount Lebanon
Zayadina.fact: The rebellions of the 1760s also often drew in rival factions among the Metawalis and the Shihab-led Druze of Mount Lebanon. Ali was the most distinguished of his brothers on the battlefield, having commanded the Zayadina and the Metawalis in numerous engagements on Daher's behalf in the early 1770s.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: As Daher was reconciling with the Ottoman authorities in _____, his sons, "getting on in age themselves, finally wanted power for themselves", according to Philipp, and renewed their rebellions
Zayadina.fact: As Daher was reconciling with the Ottoman authorities in 1774, his sons, "getting on in age themselves, finally wanted power for themselves", according to Philipp, and renewed their rebellions.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The rivalry between Ali and _____ was also intensifying by that point
Zayadina.fact: The rivalry between Ali and Uthman was also intensifying by that point. According to Joudah, Uthman "had little chance to succeed", as he had long lost his father's favor and local support save for his alliance with the Banu Saqr; Joudah proposes that Ali's main obstacle was Ahmad.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Their eldest brother, Salibi, had been killed in battle in _____ and as the two eldest remaining sons of Daher, they were each best positioned as Daher's natural successor for the Zaydani mashaykha (c
Zayadina.fact: Their eldest brother, Salibi, had been killed in battle in 1773 and as the two eldest remaining sons of Daher, they were each best positioned as Daher's natural successor for the Zaydani mashaykha (chieftainship).

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Daher rejected Ali's demand for possession of more villages and was supported by _____ during Ali's subsequent rebellion
Zayadina.fact: According to Joudah, Uthman "had little chance to succeed", as he had long lost his father's favor and local support save for his alliance with the Banu Saqr; Joudah proposes that Ali's main obstacle was Ahmad. Daher rejected Ali's demand for possession of more villages and was supported by Ahmad during Ali's subsequent rebellion.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: In the ensuing battle at Rameh on 11 July _____, Ali defeated them, shooting and wounding Ahmad in the leg and forcing their flight to Deir Hanna
Zayadina.fact: In the ensuing battle at Rameh on 11 July 1774, Ali defeated them, shooting and wounding Ahmad in the leg and forcing their flight to Deir Hanna.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: While the two were able to keep Ali at bay, Daher's finances were becoming strained and Ali was able to gain the defection of some of Daher's _____ mercenaries seeking better pay
Zayadina.fact: While the two were able to keep Ali at bay, Daher's finances were becoming strained and Ali was able to gain the defection of some of Daher's Maghrebi mercenaries seeking better pay.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Despite the frequency of the rebellions and their increasing intensity in the 1770s, _____'s sons did not attempt to end his rule or risk his life
Zayadina.fact: The modern scholar Uriel Heyd considers the sons' 1770s rebellions as caused by their "lust for power" and growing "hatred" of their octogenarian father and blamed their failure to support Daher in his final days for his fall. In Cohen's view, the growing power ambitions of Daher's sons never endangered Daher's rule, arguing that until his fall, Daher's sons shed their opposition and rallied around him when confronting external threats.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The French consul of Sidon summarized the rebellions in _____: That is how the wars he waged with his children have always ended: initially, they appear frightening because they are fought with armed
Zayadina.fact: The French consul of Sidon summarized the rebellions in 1774: That is how the wars he waged with his children have always ended: initially, they appear frightening because they are fought with armed force.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: While not denying the rebellions were genuine, _____ notes that Daher likely considered the clashes a way to provide his sons and troops regular combat experience and keep them battle ready
Zayadina.fact: Cohen affirms that these skirmishes were governed by self-imposed restrictions out of respect for family bonds, citing examples where Ali desisted from pursuing his defeated father at Rameh in 1774 and where soldiers from the opposite side rescued Daher after he had fallen from his horse and then rejoined the battle. While not denying the rebellions were genuine, Cohen notes that Daher likely considered the clashes a way to provide his sons and troops regular combat experience and keep them b...

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The French vice-consul of Acre in _____ likened the engagements to a sort of war game
Zayadina.fact: Cohen affirms that these skirmishes were governed by self-imposed restrictions out of respect for family bonds, citing examples where Ali desisted from pursuing his defeated father at Rameh in 1774 and where soldiers from the opposite side rescued Daher after he had fallen from his horse and then rejoined the battle. The French vice-consul of Acre in 1774 likened the engagements to a sort of war game.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Ali bribed _____ al-Azm, governor of Damascus, to petition the imperial authorities to sanction his rule, to no avail
Zayadina.fact: Ali bribed Muhammad Pasha al-Azm, governor of Damascus, to petition the imperial authorities to sanction his rule, to no avail.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The brothers attempted to block supplies from the countryside reaching Acre, intending to pressure _____ into quitting the city, but this had little effect
Zayadina.fact: Jazzar's first priority was subduing the Zayadina and destroying their forts. Daher's son Uthman defected to Jazzar early on in return for keeping control of Shefa-Amr and a promise to appoint him shaykh al-mashayikh (chief of chiefs) of bilad Safad, but his brother Ali, with the support of Daher's other sons Ahmad, Sa'id and Salih, remained incalcitrant and controlled all the Galilee from Tiberias and Safed in the east to Majd al-Krum and Abu Sinan in the west.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: In April _____, they raided the environs of Acre, harrying its walls and destroying part of its water mills
Zayadina.fact: In April 1776, they raided the environs of Acre, harrying its walls and destroying part of its water mills. By early June 1776, Ali had been defeated in successive battles at Majd al-Krum and Rameh, whose walls were then razed.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: By early June _____, Ali had been defeated in successive battles at Majd al-Krum and Rameh, whose walls were then razed
Zayadina.fact: In April 1776, they raided the environs of Acre, harrying its walls and destroying part of its water mills. By early June 1776, Ali had been defeated in successive battles at Majd al-Krum and Rameh, whose walls were then razed.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: With his men from Majd al-Krum, _____ and Deir Hanna, Ali launched an abortive assault on Jazzar's forces at Amqa
Zayadina.fact: As Jazzar consolidated his position in the town of Acre, Ali consolidated control over the Galilee from his capital at Safed, and, with his Druze allies, controlled the fortress villages of Tiberias, Majd al-Krum, Abu Sinan, Beit Jann, Rameh, Sajur, Bi'ina, Julis, Yirka, Nahf, Jiddin, Suhmata, Sa'sa', Deir al-Qassi and Deir Hanna. With his men from Majd al-Krum, Abu Sinan and Deir Hanna, Ali launched an abortive assault on Jazzar's forces at Amqa.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: At this point _____ was in control of the western and most of central Galilee, with the Zaydani rebels in control of the area between Deir Hanna, Safed and Tiberias
Zayadina.fact: With his men from Majd al-Krum, Abu Sinan and Deir Hanna, Ali launched an abortive assault on Jazzar's forces at Amqa. At this point Jazzar was in control of the western and most of central Galilee, with the Zaydani rebels in control of the area between Deir Hanna, Safed and Tiberias.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The first was commanded by Sa'id, the second by Ali and the third by _____
Zayadina.fact: The first was commanded by Sa'id, the second by Ali and the third by Ahmad. During the siege, Jazzar sowed divisions within Zaydani family ranks, having Ali's brother Uthman and his Bedouin supporters join in the siege, and offering safe conduct to Ahmad and Sa'id; five of Daher's sons were reported to have surrendered to Hasan Pasha al-Jaza'iri, who had returned to Acre, in July 1776.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: With 3,000, 5,000 or 12,000 soldiers (according to different estimates) and heavy guns, Jazzar besieged _____
Zayadina.fact: At this point Jazzar was in control of the western and most of central Galilee, with the Zaydani rebels in control of the area between Deir Hanna, Safed and Tiberias. With 3,000, 5,000 or 12,000 soldiers (according to different estimates) and heavy guns, Jazzar besieged Deir Hanna.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Ali refused to capitulate and while the two outer towers of _____ were captured by Jazzar and reinforcements were blocked, the Zaydani garrison held out against Jazzar's troops for weeks
Zayadina.fact: With 3,000, 5,000 or 12,000 soldiers (according to different estimates) and heavy guns, Jazzar besieged Deir Hanna. Ali refused to capitulate and while the two outer towers of Deir Hanna were captured by Jazzar and reinforcements were blocked, the Zaydani garrison held out against Jazzar's troops for weeks.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: A contemporary chronicler, Sa'id _____, noted the challenge posed by Deir Hanna: "It is not possible to describe (the extent) of the fortification (works) or the strength of the citadel"
Zayadina.fact: A contemporary chronicler, Sa'id Effendi, noted the challenge posed by Deir Hanna: "It is not possible to describe (the extent) of the fortification (works) or the strength of the citadel". Cannon fire heavily damaged Deir Hanna's walls, prompting Ali to dispatch the qadi of Safed, Isma'il Effendi (Isma'il Ibn Abd al-Qadir al-Safadi), to negotiate peace with Jazzar on his b.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Cannon fire heavily damaged _____'s walls, prompting Ali to dispatch the qadi of Safed, Isma'il Effendi (Isma'il Ibn Abd al-Qadir al-Safadi), to negotiate peace with Jazzar on his behalf
Zayadina.fact: A contemporary chronicler, Sa'id Effendi, noted the challenge posed by Deir Hanna: "It is not possible to describe (the extent) of the fortification (works) or the strength of the citadel". Cannon fire heavily damaged Deir Hanna's walls, prompting Ali to dispatch the qadi of Safed, Isma'il Effendi (Isma'il Ibn Abd al-Qadir al-Safadi), to negotiate peace with Jazzar on his behalf.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations

Zayadina.fact: A contemporary chronicler, Sa'id Effendi, noted the challenge posed by Deir Hanna: "It is not possible to describe (the extent) of the fortification (works) or the strength of the citadel". Cannon fire heavily damaged Deir Hanna's walls, prompting Ali to dispatch the qadi of Safed, Isma'il Effendi (Isma'il Ibn Abd al-Qadir al-Safadi), to negotiate peace with Jazzar on his behalf.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Deir Hanna was afterward razed by _____'s order
Zayadina.fact: Jazzar refused, insisting on direct negotiations, and the shelling of Deir Hanna resumed. Dabbur bypassed Ali and obtained promises of clemency from Jazzar for himself and his men and safe passage for their women and children, in return for surrendering the fortress and their weapons.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Ali escaped to _____, initially taking refuge in the Shihab family's fort at Niha
Zayadina.fact: Ali escaped to Mount Lebanon, initially taking refuge in the Shihab family's fort at Niha.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: He routed an army sent against him by _____ at Sa'sa'
Zayadina.fact: Afterward, Ali, learning of Jazzar's return to Acre, resumed operations against him, launching attempts to retake Tiberias and Deir Hanna and attacking villages around Safed. He routed an army sent against him by Jazzar at Sa'sa'.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: In mid-_____ 1776, an officer serving Muhammad Pasha of Damascus who had gained entry into Ali's camp struck and killed Ali, sending his head to Constantinople
Zayadina.fact: In mid-November 1776, an officer serving Muhammad Pasha of Damascus who had gained entry into Ali's camp struck and killed Ali, sending his head to Constantinople.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Remnants of the Zayadina, as well as Muhammad al-Husayn of Sahil Akka, the Metawalis and the Banu Saqr rebelled against Jazzar in late _____ but the risings were suppressed with assistance of local Dr
Zayadina.fact: Remnants of the Zayadina, as well as Muhammad al-Husayn of Sahil Akka, the Metawalis and the Banu Saqr rebelled against Jazzar in late 1778 but the risings were suppressed with assistance of local Druze sheikhs.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: At unclear points, _____ was made governor of the sanjaks of Jeddah of the Hejaz Eyalet in western Arabia and of Bursa (Hüdavendigâr) of the Hüdavendigâr Eyalet in western Anatolia
Zayadina.fact: At unclear points, Uthman was made governor of the sanjaks of Jeddah of the Hejaz Eyalet in western Arabia and of Bursa (Hüdavendigâr) of the Hüdavendigâr Eyalet in western Anatolia.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Ali's sons _____, who took up the name 'Fadil' and became a well-known author by the name Enderûnlu Fâzıl, and Hasan, who took up the name 'Kamil' were educated in the Enderun palace
Zayadina.fact: Remnants of the Zayadina, as well as Muhammad al-Husayn of Sahil Akka, the Metawalis and the Banu Saqr rebelled against Jazzar in late 1778 but the risings were suppressed with assistance of local Druze sheikhs. Ali's sons Husayn, who took up the name 'Fadil' and became a well-known author by the name Enderûnlu Fâzıl, and Hasan, who took up the name 'Kamil' were educated in the Enderun palace.

Zayadina.fact: 1789–1807), Fadil held administrative posts in Rhodes, Aleppo and Erzerum.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: These buildings improved the domestic administration and general security of the _____
Zayadina.fact: These buildings improved the domestic administration and general security of the Galilee.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The restoration and refortification of Acre and the establishment of the secondary harbor town of Haifa significantly strengthened the _____'s ties with the Mediterranean world
Zayadina.fact: The restoration and refortification of Acre and the establishment of the secondary harbor town of Haifa significantly strengthened the Galilee's ties with the Mediterranean world. The Zayadina's strong reliance on the rural populace of the Galilee for their military and political power manifested in their fortification of friendly villages across the region, most especially Deir Hanna, which together with their nearby hometown of Arraba effectively formed the family's rural capital.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: They resided in the eponymous al-_____ alley in the eastern neighborhood of Haifa
Zayadina.fact: They resided in the eponymous al-Bashir alley in the eastern neighborhood of Haifa.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Hasan was later appointed head judge of Shefa-Amr in _____–1890
Zayadina.fact: Hasan was later appointed head judge of Shefa-Amr in 1889–1890. Another of Abdallah's sons, Salah, was appointed tax collector of Acre in 1889.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Another of Abdallah's sons, Salah, was appointed tax collector of Acre in _____
Zayadina.fact: Hasan was later appointed head judge of Shefa-Amr in 1889–1890. Another of Abdallah's sons, Salah, was appointed tax collector of Acre in 1889.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Another member of the family with the name Abdallah was posted as head judge in the Beqaa Valley district in _____
Zayadina.fact: Another member of the family with the name Abdallah was posted as head judge in the Beqaa Valley district in 1914.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Both Abdallah and Abu al-Nur wielded significant influence among Haifa's _____ community
Zayadina.fact: Both Abdallah and Abu al-Nur wielded significant influence among Haifa's Muslim community.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: When Abu al-Nur banned the British vice consul from meeting with the town's Christians, the British succeeded in lobbying the Ottomans to depose him for Abdallah, who was honored by the Prince of Wale
Zayadina.fact: When Abu al-Nur banned the British vice consul from meeting with the town's Christians, the British succeeded in lobbying the Ottomans to depose him for Abdallah, who was honored by the Prince of Wales in 1862.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Other prominent members were Abdallah's brother As'ad, who left a considerable real estate fortune in _____, and Mahmud al-Zaydani (fl
Zayadina.fact: Other prominent members were Abdallah's brother As'ad, who left a considerable real estate fortune in 1871, and Mahmud al-Zaydani (fl.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The heirs of Abdallah and Abu al-Nur sold the family's main asset, a waterpowered flour mill, in _____ to local Christian merchants of the Khuri and Mudawwar families
Zayadina.fact: The heirs of Abdallah and Abu al-Nur sold the family's main asset, a waterpowered flour mill, in 1874 to local Christian merchants of the Khuri and Mudawwar families.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Nevertheless, by dint of their lineage and marriage alliances, the Bashir al-Zaydani retained their honorary status in Haifa as wujuh (dignitaries) until the end of Ottoman rule in _____
Zayadina.fact: Nevertheless, by dint of their lineage and marriage alliances, the Bashir al-Zaydani retained their honorary status in Haifa as wujuh (dignitaries) until the end of Ottoman rule in 1917.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: There, he met with Napoleon during his invasion of Palestine in _____ and they discussed allying against Jazzar
Zayadina.fact: There, he met with Napoleon during his invasion of Palestine in 1799 and they discussed allying against Jazzar.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: After the latter repulsed _____'s siege of Acre that year, Abbas and his brother Salih, who had since returned from Constantinople, left with the French and moved to Paris
Zayadina.fact: There, he met with Napoleon during his invasion of Palestine in 1799 and they discussed allying against Jazzar. After the latter repulsed Napoleon's siege of Acre that year, Abbas and his brother Salih, who had since returned from Constantinople, left with the French and moved to Paris.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Abbas returned to Nazareth, where he died in _____
Zayadina.fact: Abbas returned to Nazareth, where he died in 1811.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: His son, Husayn, was appointed mutasallim (governor) of Nazareth in _____
Zayadina.fact: His son, Husayn, was appointed mutasallim (governor) of Nazareth in 1850.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Descendants of Abbas, or more specifically the seven sons of Abbas's other son As'ad (Abbas, Ali, Kanj, Salih, Ahmad and Daher) make up the present family in _____
Zayadina.fact: Abbas returned to Nazareth, where he died in 1811. His son, Husayn, was appointed mutasallim (governor) of Nazareth in 1850.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Ali served as the third mayor of Nazareth in _____–1892
Zayadina.fact: Ali served as the third mayor of Nazareth in 1889–1892.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: He and his brother _____ held the military title of agha
Zayadina.fact: Descendants of Abbas, or more specifically the seven sons of Abbas's other son As'ad (Abbas, Ali, Kanj, Salih, Ahmad and Daher) make up the present family in Nazareth. He and his brother Abbas held the military title of agha.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Their brother Kanje, a grain merchant, held a seat on _____'s municipal council
Zayadina.fact: Descendants of Abbas, or more specifically the seven sons of Abbas's other son As'ad (Abbas, Ali, Kanj, Salih, Ahmad and Daher) make up the present family in Nazareth. Ali served as the third mayor of Nazareth in 1889–1892.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Descendants of Daher's son Sa'id acquired lands and settled in _____
Zayadina.fact: Descendants of Daher's son Sa'id acquired lands and settled in Deir Hanna.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Other descendants were reported living in Kafr Manda as early as _____
Zayadina.fact: Other descendants were reported living in Kafr Manda as early as 1852.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: After the depopulation of Damun by the Israelis in the _____ war, the descendants of Ali ibn Salih (Daher's uncle) there partly relocated to Tamra, the other part joining their kinsmen in Kafr Manda
Zayadina.fact: After the depopulation of Damun by the Israelis in the 1948 war, the descendants of Ali ibn Salih (Daher's uncle) there partly relocated to Tamra, the other part joining their kinsmen in Kafr Manda.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: Sa'id al-_____ secured Muhammad work in a gunpowder factory in Damascus and he eventually became a successful operator
Zayadina.fact: The patriarch of the family, Muhammad, was a grandson of Daher who took refuge with the Zayadina's old friends, the Shuwayki family of Damascus, to escape the Ottomans' pursuit of the Zayadina in the immediate aftermath of Daher's death. Sa'id al-Shuwayki secured Muhammad work in a gunpowder factory in Damascus and he eventually became a successful operator.

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: The family thereafter became known as 'al-_____' (the gunpowder [maker])
Zayadina.fact: The family thereafter became called 'al-Barudi' (the gunpowder [maker]). Muhammad's great-grandson, Fakhri al-Barudi (1877–1966), was a prominent Syrian nationalist politician and poet during the French Mandate period (1920–1946).

Zayadina.subject: International Relations
Zayadina.question: This assistance allowed the Zu'biyya to establish their local power in _____
Zayadina.fact: This assistance allowed the Zu'biyya to establish their local power in Ramtha.
